tool.name: DtedIndexValidate

param.name: dted_index
param.dialogReference: The GeoPackage or GeoParquet index to check: one row per cell, as Build DTED Index writes it, a catalog exports it, or an edit in a GIS left it.

param.name: dted_profile
param.dialogReference: The product profile the run will use with this index: its constants stand behind the NULL rows, so the check says what nothing supplies, and the rows are compared with them.

param.name: dted_overrides
param.dialogReference: The header overrides the run will use, the same rows as the DTED Header Overrides of the EGMTrans Tool: a header field and its value per row, counted as a source for that field. compilation_date = today is the usual row.

param.name: dted_level
param.dialogReference: The level the run will write. The index and the profile must be for it; left blank, the level of the index is taken.

tool.summary: Checks a DTED metadata index as a run with the same profile and overrides would see it: two rows for one cell, cell ids, values out of range or of the wrong form, the level, the accuracy subregions (count, order, vertices, outlines inside the cell), producer codes against FIPS 10-4, rows that disagree with a profile constant, and whether every required header field comes from the index, the profile or an override. The same check runs on the command line as "egmtrans dted-index validate INDEX".
tool.usage:
• An error stops a run before anything is written: two rows for one cell, a bad cell id, a value out of range, a level other than the one chosen, a subregion rule broken.

  • A warning does not stop a run: a required field NULL in some rows that the profile supplies, a producer code without a country prefix, a row that differs from a profile constant, an accuracy left NULL when the profile holds a number (the header will say NA).

  • With a profile, one error names every required header field that neither the index, the profile nor the overrides supplies; a row compilation_date = today in the overrides is the usual way to supply the date.

  • Run it after editing the index in ArcGIS Pro, before the EGMTrans Tool reads it.
